impact:
'shows help when no arguments provided' calls `$this->artisan('task:show')` with no `task` argument and asserts exit code 1 plus 'Not enough arguments'. In-process, Symfony's Input::validate() throws `RuntimeException: Not enough arguments (missing: "task")` (vendor/symfony/console/Input/Input.php:69) before TaskShowCommand::handle() is ever entered, so the test errors rather than failing an assertion.

The test describes real terminal behaviour — at a shell, `php artisan task:show` does print that message and exit non-zero, because the console Application catches the exception and renders it. What it does not describe is `$this->artisan()`, which lets the exception propagate.

So the command is fine and the expectation is fine; only the mechanism is wrong. Assert the throw (`$this->expectException(RuntimeException::class)` or Pest's `->throws(...)`), which is what the in-process runner can actually observe.

Found while fixing ISS-015; a different defect class from the renderer-mismatch assertions that issue covered.
title: Missing-argument test expects exit code 1, but Symfony throws before the command runs
